Before 1873, you could stare at Pest from Buda... and still be stuck for days. So how did two cities become Budapest?
On this side: Buda. Hills, a royal castle.
On that side: Pest. Flat, busy, full of merchants.
But between them ran the Danube... with no permanent bridge.
So how do you glue two cities together?
Not easily. When the river froze, even the bridge of boats was useless. The nearest real bridge? Vienna. 250 kilometres away.
The story goes... in 1820, Count Széchenyi reached this river, on his way to his father's funeral.
The ice wouldn't let him cross. He waited about a week... and missed it.
So he pushed for a permanent bridge.
Two British engineers built it. Both named Clark. Not related.
In 1849, the Chain Bridge opened. And on it, even nobles had to pay the toll.
I have to pay? To walk?
The cities grew together... and in 1873, they merged. Buda, plus Pest... Budapest.
Except... it was never just two cities.
A third town joined that day: Óbuda. Literally, Old Buda.
And nobody puts me in the name.
